_comment: STAGING AREA, NOT A HOME. Facts the phone receptionist needs that are not yet
published in Kumi's club_knowledge. Merged into the Bland knowledge base by
scripts/sync-bland-kb.mjs, which warns on every run while this file is non-empty.
Kumi has no HTTP write path for knowledge rows, so these were staged here to
unblock testing rather than wait on manual entry. They belong in Kumi's
knowledge admin: until they move, the PHONE agent knows things the WEBSITE
chatbot does not, which is exactly the drift this project set out to avoid.
Paste each topic/answer into the admin, tick public, then delete it from here.
Answers supplied by the club owner, 9 August 2026.

entries.answer: Foundry Padel is at 8613 North Crawford Street, Portland, Oregon 97203, in the St. Johns neighbourhood near Cathedral Park. If the two big rollup doors are closed, the entrance is the door just to the left of them, in the brick building. That is where the cafe, the retail space and the social space are.
There are 6 parking spots on site, and there is plenty of street parking around the club.

entries.topic: Air conditioning, heating and how warm the courts are
entries.answer: The brick building, with the cafe, retail and social space, is air conditioned. The warehouse where the courts are is not climate controlled. In winter there are heaters for the courts.

A renovation is underway. The two bathrooms on the first floor are closed at the moment, and that is where the men's and women's showers and changing rooms will be. For now there is a bathroom and a shower upstairs. It is gender neutral, a single room rather than separate ones.
Yes, there is wifi for guests. Scan the QR code at the club when you arrive and it will give you the password.
There are no formal gift cards yet, but the club can generate a voucher code for any amount you like. You can print it or write it into a card, and the player redeems it on Playtomic.
Yes, there is an online waiver, and it needs to be signed in the Playtomic app before you arrive.
The first floor is wheelchair accessible. There is no access to the upstairs.

entries.topic: Watching, spectators and just hanging out
entries.answer: Spectators are very welcome, and you do not need to be playing to come in. The social spaces are being upgraded as part of the renovation, and the club encourages people to come and hang out and watch.

entries.topic: Kids, juniors, and the minimum age
entries.answer: Kids are welcome to play with a parent, or under a parent's supervision. Under 16s cannot join beginner or high level tournaments. There are no youth courses or camps yet, but depending on the child's age some of the coaches are willing to teach juniors, so it is worth asking.

entries.topic: Buying a racket, and what the pro shop stocks
entries.answer: The pro shop sells rackets, balls and overgrips. The stock is mostly Wilson, with Babolat and Adidas as well, and rackets run from about $150 to $400. Rentals are $5 a racket, and high end demo rackets are $10.

Corporate memberships are live. There is basic information on the memberships page of the website, and the best route is the corporate inquiry form there. Monica replies with pricing and the details. Anyone who wants to talk it through in detail can be put through to Monica or Jake.
There is beer and wine at the bar, and vending machines, but no kitchen and no food menu. St. Johns has excellent food within a couple of blocks.

entries.topic: Jobs and working at the club
Coming to look around or take a tour
entries.answer: Walk in any time and there is usually someone around who can show you the place. Very early in the morning, or after 8pm, is better arranged in advance.
